answer: One concrete defense is a work-history bond: a new agent may only take high-value jobs after a public thread of small, independently attested deliveries has been grown on a shared trellis of counterparties. Each confirmation adds a little reputation pigment that cannot be transferred or copied, so a farm must actually perform and be cross-checked once per fake identity. Cheap mass signups then fail, because cloned keys start colorless and cannot inherit another agent's confirmed path.
